column1: # Places (chapter 07): the manifest every scope of proximeet-places-review runs and is judged by.
# scripts/places_review.sh builds each run's -only-testing list from this file, in this order on its
# device, and scripts/places_review_results.py checks every row against the build's logs.
# Columns (tab-separated): scope, order, device, run, bundle, seconds, test, kind.
#   scope    places = the new Places review; signal = the 16 Signal executions of build 6ab7e942
#            Continue preview now opens Places instead of "End of this preview."; regressions = the
#            (build 6ab81e22), unchanged, with its time-gated repeat. Together: 41 unique test methods and
#            43 required executions carried over, and 11 unique Places methods in 13 executions.
#            After the Places correction these 56 required executions run again. Build 1, the first
#            correction build (Codemagic 6ab8adb4, on 907d7401), passed 14 of its 15 required rows; C12
#            failed on a product issue, so the product change and the correction ran again on 808950f,
#            and nothing of build 1 counts toward the recovery. Recovery build 2 (Codemagic
#            6ab8c585873de42fcd4f1a8a, scope correction, on 808950f) passed C10-C15 on the smaller
#            iPhone; on the iPhone 17 Pro Max every run exited 65 before any test started (the test
#            runner failed to initialize for UI testing). Two builds were left, so the recovery ends
#            with gate_finish (build 3) and sweep_finish (build 4), below, on one commit whose product
#            and test files equal 808950f's; docs/verification/places-recovery-coverage.tsv names the
#            build, scope and run expected to execute every row, and scripts/places_recovery_reconcile.py
#            reconciles row by row. The places, signal, correction, sweep and regressions rows stay as
#            they were: the record of what was reviewed, and scopes that can still be run on their own.
#            correction = the recovery's correction gate, the targeted Places correction after build
#            6ab8639c (the adaptive footer, one-stage back gestures, where a stage starts), reworked after
#            build 6ab88011. On main: C3, the case that build left interrupted, first and alone, in a run
#            whose bound includes the main runner's measured first start (about 300 s); then C1 and C2;
#            then the five Signal and interaction tests whose endpoint changed, with C9, in XCTest's
#            class order. On the smaller iPhone: the recorded correction walkthrough C10 (full holds),
#            then C12-C15, then C11 alone. 15 rows, all required. The scroll diagnostic's rows C16 and
#            C17 (kind diagnostic, runs probe_main and probe_small) are removed: in build 6ab8adb4 C17
#            (smaller iPhone) ran and C16 (main) was left unrun for time; the test method
#            PlacesCorrectionTests/testScrollDiagnosticProbe stays in the test file, run by no scope.
#            sweep = the recovery's sweep, one build for what sweep_places and sweep_signal (both
#            removed) split between two: on main, P1-P6 (places_main), then S3-S6, S8-S10, S12 and S13
#            (signal_main); on the smaller iPhone P9-P13 (places_small), then S15 and S16 (signal_small).
#            22 rows, all required. It keeps the places and signal row IDs and test methods, so the builds
#            reconcile by row ID and device. It records nothing: P1 (the real journey) runs with short
#            holds in places_main instead of a recorded journey run with full holds. Its assertions are
#            the same; only its holds (at most 0.6 s each) and the recording differ. That saves the
#            journey run's own start and close on the main device, whose lane was projected, from
#            build 6ab8adb4's measured start times, to have too little margin before the deadline
#            otherwise. The recovery's walkthrough video is the correction's C10.
#            P7 = C9, P8 = C15, S1 = C4, S2 = C5, S7 = C6, S11 = C7 and S14 = C8: those earlier
#            executions are executed by the correction scope, on the same device, at the same commit,
#            by the same method in the same kind of run (short holds). The sweep and the regressions
#            scope were planned as recovery builds 3 and 4; after build 2 they are replaced by
#            gate_finish = recovery build 3, the correction gate finished. On main: C3 (correction_first),
#            then C1 and C2 (correction_main), then C4, C5, C9, C6, C7 and C8 (correction_signal): the
#            nine correction rows that build 2's main device never started, with the correction scope's
#            row IDs, tests, runs and bounds (9 rows, required); then S3, S4, S5, S6 and S8 (signal_main_a,
#            kind extra). On the smaller iPhone: P9-P13 (places_small), then S15 and S16 (signal_small),
#            both kind extra. C10-C15 passed in build 2 and are not rerun. It records nothing.
#            sweep_finish = recovery build 4. On main: P1-P6, S9, S10, S12 and S13 (places_signal_main;
#            P1, the real journey, with short holds and unrecorded, as in the sweep), then M1-M3
#            (birthday_wristband_main). On device B, the clone of main: M4-M13 (pass_wristband_b; the
#            regressions scope ran them on main, the same model and runtime), B1 (paste_b), B10-B13
#            (welcome_b), then B15 (hardware_keys_b), last on its device because it sends hardware key
#            events. 29 rows, all required. It records nothing.
#            Not run in builds 2-4: B2-B9 (the Guest List's regressions_b tests), later run in
#            regression_finish (build 5; B2 again in regression_repair, build 6), and the optional
#            repeat B14, which no recovery build runs (pending). Every new row keeps the row ID and the
#            test method of the earlier row it runs again.
#   device   main = the selected iPhone 17 Pro Max; b = device B, its clone (same model and runtime);
#            small = a smaller installed iPhone. A scope uses main and one other device, and the two
#            run in parallel: regressions and sweep_finish use main and b, every other scope main and
#            small; except the room scopes (room, room_regression, room_regression_main,
#            room_regression_small and room_all), which run ONE SIMULATOR AT A TIME: the smaller iPhone
#            boots, and its runs start, only after the selected simulator's runs end and it is shut
#            down; a room build with no selected row on main (room_regression_small, or a row filter
#            without main rows) never boots main (it is shut down if it is booting) and boots the smaller
#            iPhone at once, alone. Every test with 440-point pixel anchors runs on main (or b, the same model). The
#            signal scope's former device-B tests run on main, which is the same model and runtime.
#   run      one bounded xcodebuild test-without-building; within a run XCTest orders the tests by
#            class, then by name. A run named "journey" is recorded and alone, with full holds (places:
#            the full journey; correction: C10; room and room_all: the Room journey R1; the sweep,
#            gate_finish, sweep_finish, room_regression, room_regression_main and room_regression_small
#            every other run uses short holds. A run whose test runner fails to initialize for UI
#            testing before any test starts (build 6ab8c585), or whose simulator is not found, is run
#            once more after the device is ready; that is an infrastructure rerun, not a test retry.
#   seconds  the run's natural time bound; the build's deadline can shorten it.
#   kind     required = must execute once and pass; repeat = a planned second execution of a
#            required test from a fresh app and test runner, run only if the time budget allows both
#            it and the run after it; it is not a unique test and not a retry, and if it runs it must pass;
#            extra = a run that starts only when its bound plus 60 s is left before the deadline (its
#            infrastructure rerun too); if it runs it must pass, and it is listed as not run (time
#            budget) otherwise; a passed extra counts toward the row-level reconciliation like a
#            required execution of the same test on the same device class; diagnostic = like extra in when it
#            starts, but its outcome is reported and never counts toward a verdict (no row uses it since
#            the scroll probe's rows C16 and C17 were removed).
# Automatic retries are off in every scope. A failed, skipped, interrupted or missing required
# regression_finish (recovery build 5, after build 4 ran out of time): the 16 earlier rows no recovery
#            build had verified: P3, P6 and M2 (interrupted in build 4), P1, S9, S10, S12 and S13 (never
#            started in build 4) and B2-B9 (never scheduled). Same row IDs, test methods and device class
#            as the rows they run again; P1 keeps its short holds, unrecorded. Its device column is a
#            PREFERENCE: the scope's runs form one shared queue for the two iPhone 17 Pro Max simulators
#            (main and device B, its clone: one device class). Each lane takes its own next run, and
#            when it has none left it takes the other lane's LAST unstarted run, so a lane that is slow
#            (build 4's main simulator ran about 2.7-7x slower per step for its whole run) cannot strand the
#            rest. Where a run actually ran is recorded in runs.txt and judged there. Neither lane starts
#            until both devices report their boot finished; XCTest's execution time allowance is 600 s
#            (maximum 660 s) for this scope, so a slow but progressing test is not cut off at 300 s.
# regression_repair (recovery build 6): an evidence-driven repair of build 5's one failure. B2 failed there
#            when an XCTest accessibility query stalled for 36 s inside a 5-s wait for the Guest List's
#            headline (the headline was correct when read); build 5's host telemetry showed 0% idle CPU in
#            29 of 34 samples, sampler intervals up to 99 s, XCTest step stalls of 10-43 s on both lanes,
#            and at the stall itself a blocked host (330 processes stuck, 55% idle; mechanism unknown).
#            The repair is a load-reduction hypothesis: B2 runs alone on the selected
#            iPhone 17 Pro Max, with no second simulator booted. It is a disclosed repeated execution, not a
#            retry: build 5's failure stands in the reconciliation (failures win).
# room (chapter 08, the Room candidate; docs/verification/room-mac-review.md): RoomReviewTests' 13
#            methods, all on the iPhone 17 Pro Max, then testLargestTextKeepsRoomReachable again on the
#            smaller iPhone (R14). R1, the real journey from Welcome through Common Ground's explanation
#            into the Room and back to Places, is the recorded run: alone, first, full holds, recorded from
#            before the app's launch and delivered unedited (its ROOM_WALKTHROUGH_START marker lets the VPS
#            trim it). R2, the captures of the 15 states, 8 overlays and 4 report variants (about 27 direct
#            launches), is alone in room_capture, so the longest test has its own bound; R3-R13 follow in
#            room_main in XCTest's order. Nothing Room has run on a Mac, so the bounds are estimates from
#            the nearest measured tests (Places build 6ab8639c: the recorded journey 187.9 s, the seven
#            screens 73.7 s for 7 launches; the recovery: 107.2 s): R1 about 250-400 s, R2 about 280-410 s,
#            R3-R13 about 500-1000 s together, R14 about 100-160 s; each bound adds the runner's start (up to
#            about 340 s for the first) and close. XCTest's allowance is 600 s (maximum 660 s) in every room
#            scope: in room and room_all because R2 would sit near 300 s; in room_regression and its halves
#            because P1 now takes two Room detours (near 200 s) and build 4 once ended a test of about 145 s
#            at the 300-s allowance on a slow host. 14 rows, 13 unique methods, all required.
# room_regression: the Places rows Room's integration touches, the recommended minimal rerun set (entry
#            and return, category, eligibility, the age gate, the footers and the Signal boundary): P1,
#            P2, P4 and C1-C9 on the iPhone 17 Pro Max, C10-C15 and P9-P13 on the smaller iPhone, each with
#            its earlier row ID, test method and device; short holds, nothing recorded (C10, the
#            correction's recorded walkthrough, runs unrecorded here). Runs and bounds from the latest
#            measured passes: rr_places_main (C1, C2, C3, P2, P4, P1: 666 s measured, 1080 s bound, the
#            first run, so its bound includes the runner's first start), rr_signal_main (C4, C5, C9, C6-C8:
#            367 s, 600 s, correction_signal's run), rr_places_small (C15, P9-P13: 614 s, 900 s),
#            rr_correction_small (C10, C12-C14: 253 s, 600 s) and rr_correction_small_b (C11 alone, as in
#            the correction scope: 63 s, 240 s). 1964 s of tests measured in the recovery's two-simulator
#            builds (about 1710 s at each row's fastest measured pace), so with its five runner starts,
#            the smaller iPhone's first boot and about 200 s before the first test it is at the edge of
#            the 45-minute workflow's 2340-s deadline, and past it when run one simulator at a time:
#            room_regression_main and room_regression_small (below) split it by lane. 23 rows, all required.
# room_all:  room's rows, then room_regression's, with the same runs, bundles and bounds, for one build if
#            the time allows. At the estimates above it needs about 3800-4900 s of UI time and does not
#            fit proximeet-room-review-45 (2340 s): run room and room_regression as two builds instead.
# room_regression_main: room_regression's 12 iPhone 17 Pro Max rows, copied under the same row IDs, test
#            methods, devices, runs, bundles and bounds: C1, C2, C3, P2, P4 and P1 (rr_places_main), then C4,
#            C5, C9, C6, C7 and C8 (rr_signal_main). 1034 s of tests measured (666 s and 368 s), so it fits a
#            35-minute build (1740 s) with room to spare: room_regression split by lane, because the whole set
#            (1964 s of tests, run one simulator at a time) does not fit one 45-minute build. 12 rows, all
# room_regression_small: room_regression's 11 smaller-iPhone rows, copied the same way: C15 and P9-P13
#            (rr_places_small), then C10, C12, C13 and C14 (rr_correction_small), then C11 alone
#            (rr_correction_small_b). 930 s of tests measured (614 s, 253 s and 63 s). It has no main row, so
#            the iPhone 17 Pro Max is never booted: the smaller iPhone boots in destinations, alone, behind the
# All five run one simulator at a time (the device column above) and keep every recovery rule: no
# retries, infrastructure reruns only for a run that started no test. None of their results counts
# toward the Places recovery, which is frozen at 808950f.
# PLACES_ROW_FILTER (optional run input, any scope): comma-separated row IDs of the chosen scope, for
#            example R3,R9,R14. The source gate accepts it only if every ID matches ^[A-Z][0-9]{1,2}$,
#            belongs to the scope and appears once, and records it (row_filter= in its result, and
#            build/artifacts/metadata/places-row-filter.txt). Then only the selected rows run: each keeps
#            its run, order and device; a run with no selected row is skipped whole (the recorded journey
#            too, unless its row is selected); the results, the verdict and the package judge and count
#            only the selected rows, name them and say the others were not part of the build. Unset, every
#            row of the scope runs, as before.
